message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta. Noise violations are usually handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** and/or the **Code Enforcement Office** rather than directly by the city council. Here’s how you can report it: | Step | What to Do | Contact Details | |------|------------|-----------------| | 1 | Identify the type of noise issue (e.g., loud music after hours, construction noise, barking dogs, etc.). | — | | 2 | Gather details: location (street address or intersection), time(s) of disturbance, description of the source, and any evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings). | — | | 3 | File a complaint online via the City of Atlanta’s official portal. | **Website:** https://www.atlantaga.gov/311
Search “Noise Complaint” or “Code Enforcement.” | | 4 | If you prefer phone, call the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line at **404‑656‑4000** and ask to speak with the Code Enforcement or Public Safety Officer handling noise complaints. | **Phone:** 404‑656‑4000 (non‑emergency) | | 5 | For urgent or ongoing disturbances, you may also dial **911** if you believe the situation poses an immediate safety risk. | **Emergency:** 911 | | 6 | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy for follow‑up. | — | ### Additional Tips - **Timing matters:** Many noise ordinances have specific “quiet hours” (often 10 p.m.–7 a.m.) during which certain activities are prohibited. Make sure your complaint falls within those hours. - **Documentation helps:** Attach photos, videos, or audio clips when submitting online; this gives officers a clearer picture of the violation. - **Follow up:** If the problem persists after a reasonable period (usually a few days), you can call back using the reference number to check on the status of your complaint. Feel free to let me know if you’d like help drafting the complaint text or navigating the online form!
